routes.title: Landlord Reference Letter
routes.description: A landlord reference letter is a current or former landlord's signed statement about one tenancy: the address, the dates, the rent, the payment record, and whether they would rent to you again. Build one in the browser below, from either side of the request.

routes.title: Rental Verification Form
routes.description: A rental verification form is the fixed field sheet a new landlord or housing agency sends to a previous landlord: dates, rent, balance owed, late count, notices, would-rent-again. Complete one below — with the tenant authorization that is the reason most of them come back blank.

routes.title: Employment Verification Form
routes.description: An employment verification form is a fixed field sheet an employer completes and returns directly to whoever asked for it. Which form you need is decided by the requester, not by you — a mortgage file, a VA file, and a benefits office each require their own and none accepts a substitute.
routes.secondary_cta: See the Income + Employment Letter Kit

routes.title: Employment Verification Letter Template
routes.description: Six employment verification letter templates, one for each requester that asks for one: a landlord, a lender, a benefits agency, an immigration filing, a contractor's client, and a former employer. Fill the fields in once below and the generator writes whichever version you need.
routes.secondary_cta: See the Income + Employment Letter Kit

routes.title: Proof of Employment Letter
routes.description: A proof of employment letter is the weakest item in the employment evidence stack and the easiest one to obtain. This page ranks the eight things reviewers accept as proof, shows where the letter sits among them, and gives you what to attach so the letter holds.
routes.primary_cta: Build my proof of employment packet
routes.secondary_cta: See the Income + Employment Letter Kit

routes.title: Letter of Explanation Template
routes.description: One letter of explanation template, five sentences long, that adapts to any condition you have been asked to explain. Fill it in below and the generator produces the full letter, a short single-question version, and the covering email it travels in.
routes.secondary_cta: See the Letter of Explanation Kit

routes.title: Letter of Explanation for a Mortgage
routes.description: Underwriters do not ask for letters of explanation at random. Eight standard conditions generate almost all of them, and each one needs a different set of facts. This page maps the condition wording to what the letter has to contain and what has to travel with it.
routes.secondary_cta: See the Loan Prep Letter Kit

routes.title: Letter of Explanation Sample
routes.description: Six complete letters of explanation, filled in end to end rather than left as skeletons — a gifted deposit, a medical late payment, a four-month employment gap, a dismissed eviction filing, overdrafts during a payroll change, and one that was rejected, annotated with why.
routes.primary_cta: See the Letter of Explanation Kit
routes.secondary_cta: Use the free Letter Writing Studio

routes.title: How to Write a Letter of Explanation
routes.description: Six sentences, each doing one job. This page takes a letter of explanation apart sentence by sentence, says what each one is for, shows the version people write instead, and rewrites one weak letter line by line into one that works.
routes.primary_cta: Use the free Letter Writing Studio
routes.secondary_cta: See the Letter of Explanation Kit

routes.title: Goodwill Letter for Credit: Which Items It Can Reach
routes.description: A goodwill letter is a courtesy request to the company that reported the item. That single fact decides where it can work and where it cannot, and most goodwill letters are sent to accounts it was never able to reach.
routes.secondary_cta: Use the free Letter Writing Studio

routes.title: Rental Application Letter
routes.description: A leasing agent gives an application about thirty seconds. A rental application letter is worth writing only when something in your file will stop them at second twelve — a thin credit file, a broken lease, an income that does not look like a salary. This page is about what to write in that case.
